title: Private Console — Mesh Connectivity Inspector (compact tenant panel)
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Design a compact, information-dense inspector panel for the Private Console that surfaces tenant-level mesh connectivity, recent path health, and safe rollback actions. This panel should live as a collapsible strip in the tenant overview and expand into a transient overlay when operators need details. It must be usable by SREs and Platform Engineers to make fast triage decisions (isolate region, trigger rollback, estimate cost impact) without drilling into multiple screens.

Scope: initial MVP for single-tenant view, covers cross-region connectivity map (simplified), last-5-heartbeats visualization, top-3 failure signals (e.g., packet loss, high retransmit rate, control-plane lag), suggested mitigations (restart agent, reroute traffic to region B, initiate rolling upgrade rollback), and a compact cost delta estimator showing estimated additional egress and reserved capacity cost for failover.

Out-of-scope: full multi-tenant graph, packet-level trace replay, deep topology editor. Those will be follow-ups if MVP is validated.
acceptance_criteria: Compact panel fits within 340px height in tenant overview in collapsed state
Panel expands to overlay with per-path details and last-5-heartbeat sparkline
Top-3 signals are algorithmically ranked and human-readable (label + severity color)
Quick actions available: Open runbook, Trigger safe rollback (requires two-step confirm), Route traffic to alternate region (preview cost delta)
Design handoff artifacts (Figma frames, interaction spec) provided and validated by ENG lead
Analytics events defined for expand/collapse, action clicks, and confirm steps
decisions: Show only top-3 signals by default to keep surface scannable — full list accessible in expanded overlay
Cost estimator shows a conservative 95th-percentile delta pulled from cost-service rather than live billing to avoid surprising numbers
Rollback action will be a controlled two-step flow that triggers a canary first (safety requirement from Eng) — design includes both canary and global rollback options
Compact visual language uses small sparklines + status pill (green/amber/red) rather than large heatmaps to preserve density
Panel will default to collapsed in tenant overview; tenants with active incidents auto-expand up to 30 seconds after page load
constraints_and_risks: Backend needs new summary API (ENG-28901) to drive top-3 signals and cost estimate — latency and rate limits need to be validated
Security teams require audit logs for rollback and routing actions — UI must surface confirmation and note that actions are audited
Mobile and very narrow viewports will show only the status pill and an overflow menu linking to full overlay
Cost estimator accuracy limited until cost-service supports per-tenant reserved-capacity breakdown (work in separate ENG ticket)
handoff_notes: Export Figma components: InspectorStrip, SignalRow, CostDeltaFlyout, ConfirmRollbackModal
Provide CSS token mapping and accessibility text for each actionable element
Include interactions: hover states, keyboard focus order, aria labels for screen reader support
Tracked implementation tasks: client-side expand/collapse animation, API integration for /v1/tenants/{id}/mesh-summary, telemetry events (analytics)
Suggested implementation priority: render skeleton first, then populate signals, then cost delta (cost call can be delayed)
